content.title: Powers of i and Complex Conjugates
content.overview: This lesson covers the cyclical nature of the imaginary unit i and the properties of complex conjugates. You will learn to simplify high powers of i and use the conjugate product rule to transform complex expressions into real numbers.
learning_objectives: Simplify any power of i using the cycle of four.
Identify the complex conjugate of a given complex number.
Apply the conjugate product rule (a + bi)(a - bi) = a^2 + b^2 to simplify expressions.
Combine simplified real and imaginary components into standard form x + yi.

sections.title: The Imaginary Unit and the Cycle of i
sections.content: The imaginary unit i is defined as the square root of -1, meaning i^2 = -1. Powers of i follow a repeating cycle of four values: i^1 = i, i^2 = -1, i^3 = -i, and i^4 = 1. To simplify any power i^n, divide the exponent n by 4 and look at the remainder. If the remainder is 1, the result is i; if 2, the result is -1; if 3, the result is -i; and if 0 (or divisible by 4), the result is 1.

sections.title: Complex Conjugates and the Product Rule
sections.content: For any complex number a + bi, its complex conjugate is a - bi. The conjugate is formed by changing the sign of the imaginary part only. When you multiply a complex number by its conjugate, the result is always a real number. The formula is (a + bi)(a - bi) = a^2 + b^2. Note that because i^2 = -1, the middle terms cancel out and the subtraction of (bi)^2 becomes the addition of b^2.

sections.title: Combining Conjugates and Powers
sections.content:
ACT problems often combine these two concepts. The strategy is to simplify the conjugate product into a single real number first, then reduce the power of i to its simplest form (1, i, -1, or -i), and finally combine them into the standard form x + yi.

![A flow chart showing the steps to simplify complex expressions involving conjugates and powers of i.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/cce5990c-75ca-4903-9299-525095b4b24a-1786505476425-728.webp)

worked_examples.question: Simplify the expression (5 + 2i)(5 - 2i) + i^38.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Identify the conjugate product (5 + 2i)(5 - 2i). Using the rule a^2 + b^2, we get 5^2 + 2^2 = 25 + 4 = 29. Step 2: Simplify the power i^38. Divide 38 by 4. 38 = (4 * 9) + 2. The remainder is 2. Therefore, i^38 = i^2 = -1. Step 3: Combine the results. 29 + (-1) = 28. The final simplified value is 28.

worked_examples.question: What is the standard form of (2 - 3i)(2 + 3i) - i^15?
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Calculate the conjugate product (2 - 3i)(2 + 3i). a=2, b=3. a^2 + b^2 = 2^2 + 3^2 = 4 + 9 = 13. Step 2: Simplify i^15. 15 divided by 4 gives a remainder of 3. i^15 = i^3 = -i. Step 3: Combine the results, paying attention to the subtraction sign in the original problem: 13 - (-i) = 13 + i.

common_mistakes: Mistakenly using a^2 - b^2 for the conjugate product instead of a^2 + b^2.
Forgetting that i^2 = -1 when simplifying powers.
Changing the sign of the real part instead of the imaginary part when finding a conjugate.
Miscalculating the remainder when dividing the exponent by 4.
exam_tips: If the exponent of i is even, the result must be 1 or -1. If the exponent is odd, the result must be i or -i.
The product of a complex number and its conjugate is always a non-negative real number.
Quick check: i^100 is 1 because 100 is divisible by 4.
content.recap: To master complex numbers on the ACT, remember the cycle of i (i, -1, -i, 1) and the conjugate product rule (a + bi)(a - bi) = a^2 + b^2. Always reduce powers of i using the remainder of the exponent divided by 4 and combine like terms to reach the final x + yi form.

knowledge_claims.content: The imaginary unit i is defined such that i^2 = -1.
Powers of i cycle every four terms: i^1=i, i^2=-1, i^3=-i, and i^4=1.
To simplify i^n, divide n by 4 and use the remainder to determine the value: 1=i, 2=-1, 3=-i, 0=1.
The complex conjugate of a + bi is a - bi.
The product of a complex number and its conjugate (a + bi)(a - bi) equals a^2 + b^2.
The product of any complex number and its conjugate results in a real number.
A common error is calculating (a + bi)(a - bi) as a^2 - b^2, forgetting that i^2 changes the sign to addition.
If an exponent of i is divisible by 4, the expression simplifies to 1.
If an exponent of i is even but not divisible by 4, the expression simplifies to -1.
When simplifying (a + bi)(a - bi), ensure the result has no 'i' term remaining.
To simplify (a + bi)(a - bi) + i^n, first calculate the real sum a^2 + b^2, then add the reduced value of i^n.
Unlike the real part 'a', the imaginary part 'bi' changes sign when forming a complex conjugate.
